name: Peter A. Rozman
identity: Assistant Professor of Neurosurgery, NYU Grossman School of Medicine; stereotactic and functional / epilepsy neurosurgeon at the NYU Langone Comprehensive Epilepsy Center and Center for Neuromodulation (also NYC Health + Hospitals / Bellevue).
bio: Peter Rozman is a young academic functional neurosurgeon at NYU Langone who focuses on epilepsy, movement disorders, and pain. He is fellowship-trained across the modern minimally invasive functional toolkit, including laser interstitial thermal therapy (LITT), robot-assisted stereo-EEG (SEEG), radiofrequency ablation, and MR-guided high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU). His research centers on intracranial electrophysiology of epilepsy networks, particularly temporal-pole and temporopolar seizure onset. He represents the incoming generation of NYU functional surgeons carrying the LITT program forward.
training: Harvard Medical School (MD) · Neurosurgery residency, NYU Grossman School of Medicine / NYU Langone · Fellowship in stereotactic & functional neurosurgery and epilepsy surgery, Emory University · pedigree note: Harvard MD, NYU-trained, Emory functional/epilepsy fellowship — strong academic-functional lineage.
litt_exposure: Strong, direct. Claims show litt_perf 8 in the NeuroBlate ("our equipment") cohort, alongside SEEG (9) and epilepsy craniotomy (9). Explicitly fellowship-trained in LITT at Emory and lists laser ablation among his core minimally invasive techniques. An active NeuroBlate performer.
wheelhouse: Epilepsy surgery, SEEG/robotic electrode implantation, LITT ablation, DBS/neuromodulation, movement disorders and pain; temporal-lobe and temporopolar epilepsy.
kol_note: Emerging, not yet a national KOL. Early-career (recently fellowship-trained); building a publication record in SEEG/temporopolar epilepsy. A high-value relationship to grow as he ramps NeuroBlate volume, but limited podium/authorship footprint so far.

recent_papers.note: Multi-author SEEG methods/outcomes study with Rozman as a co-author; directly adjacent to LITT epilepsy targeting though the paper itself is about SEEG localization, not ablation.

name: Dimitris G. Placantonakis
identity: Professor of Neurosurgery (and Cell Biology), NYU Grossman School of Medicine; surgical neuro-oncologist and Director of the Neurosurgical Laboratory for Stem Cell Research at NYU Langone (also NYC Health + Hospitals / Bellevue).
bio: Dimitris Placantonakis is a senior physician-scientist and surgical neuro-oncologist at NYU Langone specializing in gliomas/glioblastoma, pituitary tumors, meningiomas, and brain metastases. He is a leading academic adopter of LITT for brain tumors, pioneering awake laser ablation for tumors in eloquent cortex and combining LITT with neoadjuvant PD1 immune-checkpoint blockade for recurrent high-grade glioma. As an MD-PhD he runs a well-funded glioma stem-cell laboratory (GPR133 and glioblastoma biology). He was a site investigator in Monteris's LAANTERN NeuroBlate registry, making him one of the strongest tumor-LITT champions in the region.
training: NYU School of Medicine, Medical Scientist Training Program (MD, PhD, 2003) · Neurosurgery internship Weill Cornell, residency Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center / Weill Cornell (NewYork-Presbyterian), completed 2010 · Postdoctoral fellowship in human embryonic stem-cell biology with Lorenz Studer & Viviane Tabar at MSKCC · pedigree note: NYU MSTP + Cornell/MSK neurosurgery + Studer/Tabar stem-cell training — elite physician-scientist lineage.
litt_exposure: Strong, direct and thought-leading. Claims show litt_perf 5 in the NeuroBlate ("our equipment") cohort plus mets/RN volume (8). Multiple peer-reviewed LITT publications (awake laser ablation technique; LITT+neoadjuvant PD1 for recurrent HGG; LITT penumbra cell-death biology) and named co-author on the Monteris LAANTERN NeuroBlate glioblastoma registry analysis. A NeuroBlate power user and evangelist.
wheelhouse: Surgical neuro-oncology: glioblastoma/glioma, brain metastases, pituitary and skull-base tumors, meningioma; awake mapping, LITT/laser ablation, focused ultrasound, tubular retractor and endoscopic approaches; glioma stem-cell research.
kol_note: Yes — genuine tumor-LITT KOL. Publishes on LITT technique and LITT+immunotherapy combinations, directs an NIH-caliber glioma stem-cell lab, and was a LAANTERN (NeuroBlate) registry investigator. Ideal reference user, podium speaker, and clinical-evidence partner for NeuroBlate in neuro-oncology.

name: Donato R. Pacione
identity: Assistant Professor of Neurosurgery, NYU Grossman School of Medicine; skull-base and complex-spine neurosurgeon, NYU Langone Pituitary Center (joined faculty 2013).
bio: Donato Pacione is a skull-base and complex-spine neurosurgeon at NYU Langone who focuses on pituitary adenomas, meningiomas, craniopharyngiomas, schwannomas, chordomas, and metastatic lesions, with an emphasis on minimally invasive endoscopic endonasal and MRI-guided techniques. He graduated as medical-school valedictorian and AOA in 2006 and has co-authored roughly 90 peer-reviewed papers, concentrated in endoscopic endonasal skull-base surgery, antibiotic prophylaxis, and open-vs-endonasal anatomic approaches. His practice is anatomically centered on the skull base and spine rather than the deep-seated or eloquent parenchymal targets where LITT is typically used.
training: Medical school (MD, 2006; valedictorian, Alpha Omega Alpha) · Neurosurgery residency followed by joining the NYU faculty practice in 2013; subspecialty focus in skull-base and complex spine surgery · pedigree note: specific medical-school, residency, and fellowship institutions not verified in this pass — stated facts limited to valedictorian/AOA 2006 and NYU faculty since 2013.
litt_exposure: No evidence of direct LITT experience. Claims classify him as a LITT-naïve craniotomy surgeon (tumor_cranio 1, mets_rn 2); his documented practice and publications are skull-base/endonasal and spine, with no laser-ablation footprint.
wheelhouse: Skull-base surgery (pituitary adenoma, meningioma, craniopharyngioma, chordoma, schwannoma), endoscopic endonasal approaches, complex/deformity spine, metastatic skull-base disease.
kol_note: Recognized skull-base/spine surgeon and prolific co-author (~90 papers, endonasal skull base), but not a LITT voice. Any influence would be as a referrer or intracranial-tumor colleague, not an ablation champion.

recent_papers.journal: Journal of Neurological Surgery Part B: Skull Base
recent_papers.note: Endonasal infection-prevention study; representative of his skull-base focus, no LITT relevance.

candidacy.rationale: Anatomic-fit is weak: his caseload is skull-base/endonasal and complex spine, whereas NeuroBlate's sweet spots are deep/eloquent tumors, metastases with radiation necrosis, and epilepsy foci — areas largely covered at NYU by Placantonakis and the functional team. He does see meningiomas and metastatic lesions (some of which can be LITT candidates), and he already embraces MRI-guided, minimally invasive technology, so he is technology-receptive. But with LITT champions already entrenched in his own department, he is more likely a referral source into the NeuroBlate program than a new personal adopter. Prioritize below the functional/neuro-onc naive targets.

name: Dennis London
identity: Assistant Professor of Neurosurgery, NYU Grossman School of Medicine; stereotactic & functional neurosurgeon at NYU Langone's Center for Neuromodulation (also NYC Health + Hospitals).
bio: Dennis London is a newly appointed functional/neuromodulation neurosurgeon at NYU Langone who treats movement disorders (Parkinson's disease, essential tremor, dystonia), epilepsy, and select psychiatric conditions. He is trained in the full functional armamentarium — DBS, responsive neurostimulation (RNS), MR-guided focused ultrasound, laser ablation, and robotic/MRI-guided procedures — having just completed a stereotactic & functional fellowship at Stanford. His research background is in human single-neuron electrophysiology of the subthalamic nucleus and action planning in Parkinson's disease. As an early-career functional surgeon at a NeuroBlate site, he is a prime LITT growth target.
training: Princeton University (A.B., Molecular Biology / Quantitative & Computational Neuroscience, summa cum laude, 2014) · New York University School of Medicine (MD, 2017) · Neurosurgery residency, NYU Grossman School of Medicine (2017–2024) · Fellowship in Stereotactic & Functional Neurosurgery, Stanford University (2025) · pedigree note: Princeton → NYU MD → NYU neurosurgery → Stanford functional — strong functional/academic pedigree.
litt_exposure: LITT-naïve in claims (epi_cranio 1; classified LITT-naïve craniotomy surgeon) — expected given he only entered independent practice in 2025. However, he lists laser ablation among his trained modalities from his Stanford functional fellowship, so he has hands-on exposure but no independent NeuroBlate case volume yet.
wheelhouse: Stereotactic & functional neurosurgery: DBS, RNS, focused ultrasound, laser ablation for epilepsy/movement disorders; drug-resistant epilepsy; single-neuron electrophysiology / neural-circuit research.
kol_note: Not yet a KOL — early career, but strong research credentials (eLife single-neuron STN work) and an academic functional platform make him a rising voice worth cultivating early.

recent_papers.title: Distinct population code for movement kinematics and changes of ongoing movements in human subthalamic nucleus
recent_papers.note: First-author human STN single-neuron study (DBS-implant patients). High-caliber functional-neuroscience work but subject is movement planning, not LITT.

candidacy.rationale: Best LITT-adoption fit among the NYU naive cohort. He is a dedicated stereotactic/functional and epilepsy surgeon — exactly the profile that drives LITT ablation of mesial-temporal foci, hypothalamic hamartomas, and deep lesions — and he is already trained in laser ablation from his Stanford fellowship, so the clinical and technical barrier is low. As a brand-new independent surgeon (practice started 2025) building volume at an established NeuroBlate site, he is choosing his platform habits now; early engagement, proctoring, and case support could make NeuroBlate his default. Pair with Rozman/Placantonakis as internal champions.
